easy.def: To stretch out your hand to get something.
examples: I reach for the book.
He cannot reach the shelf.
Reach up high.

more.def: To stretch out your arm to touch or get something.
examples: She reached for the top shelf.
The baby reached out to grab my finger.
I cannot reach the jar on the top shelf.
We reach the beach at noon.
The train reached the station.
When will you reach home?

more.def: To arrive at a place, or to get as far as a certain point.
examples: We reached the top of the mountain at noon.
The hikers reached the camp before dark.
The water in the tub reached my knees.

easy.def: To look at words and know what they say.
examples: I read a book.
She reads to me.
Can you read this?

more.def: To look at written words and understand them, or to say them aloud.
examples: Our teacher reads a chapter to us every afternoon.
I read the whole book in one weekend.
Can you read the sign on the other side of the street?

easy.def: Looked at words and knew what they said.
examples: I read the book.
She read it last night.
We read that story.

more.def: Looked at written words and understood them, in the time before now.
examples: I read that book last summer, and I loved it.
She read the letter twice before she answered.
We read about volcanoes in science class yesterday.
I am ready for school.
Dinner is ready.
Are you ready?

more.def: Prepared and able to do something right away.
examples: The runners are ready at the starting line.
Are you ready for tomorrow's spelling test?
The cookies will be ready in ten minutes.
Is the dragon real?
That is a real bird.
It was a real surprise.

more.def: Existing in fact, and not imagined or fake.
examples: The story is made up, but the dinosaur bones are real.
This is a real diamond, not a piece of glass.
Is the snake in the cage real or made of rubber?
Dreams are not reality.
The reality is different.
She faced reality.

more.def: What is real and true, not imagined.
examples: He woke up and returned to reality.
The reality is that we need to leave now.
The story is a mix of fantasy and reality.
I realized I forgot my hat.
She realized it was Friday.
He realizes his mistake.

more.def: To understand something clearly, often suddenly.
examples: I realized I had left my lunch at home.
She realized the dog had been hiding under the table all along.
Do you realize how late it is?
I am really happy.
It is really cold.
She really tried.

more.def: Very much, or in fact, when something is true.
examples: The mountain is really high, so we took a long break.
Did you really see a shooting star?
I am really sorry that I broke your cup.
What is the reason?
She had a good reason.
I know the reason.

more.def: The cause of something, or an explanation for why it happens.
examples: The reason the grass is wet is that it rained last night.
He had a good reason for being late to class.
Tell me the reason you chose that book.
I recall the day.
Can you recall her name?
He recalled the song.

more.def: To bring something back into your mind, to remember it.
examples: I can recall the day we first met.
She could not recall where she had put her keys.
He recalled the words to the song.

easy.def: To get something that is sent or given.
examples: I receive mail.
She received a gift.
He received a letter.

more.def: To get something that is given or sent to you.
examples: I received a postcard from my cousin.
She received a prize for her painting.
We receive the newspaper every morning.

easy.def: To know someone or something because you have seen it before.
examples: I recognize that dog. It lives next door.
I recognize your voice.
The dog recognized me.

more.def: To know who or what something is because you have seen or heard it before.
examples: I did not recognize my cousin with his new haircut.
She recognized the song after two notes.
Babies learn to recognize their parents' faces.

easy.def: To say that something is good.
examples: I recommend this book.
She recommended a good movie.
The teacher recommended a book.

more.def: To suggest that someone should choose something because it is good.
examples: I recommend the soup, which is very tasty.
My librarian recommended a book about whales.
He recommended a good place to eat.
She set a new record in the race.
The tall tower broke the record.
He holds the swimming record.

more.def: The best score or result that anyone has reached, such as the fastest time.
examples: She set a new school record in the long jump.
The tower holds the record for the tallest building in the city.
He broke the swimming record by one second.
The nurse keeps a record of my height.
The teacher keeps a record of homework.
Keep a record of what you read.

more.def: A written account of facts or events that is kept so people can look at it later.
examples: The school keeps a record of every student's height.
Scientists keep a careful record of the weather.
My grandmother has a record of our family's history.
I record my voice.
Let's record a song.
Dad recorded the game.

more.def: To save sound or pictures so that they can be heard or seen again.
examples: The band recorded a new song in the studio.
She recorded the frogs singing at the pond.
Dad recorded my piano show on his phone.

easy.def: To use old things again to make new things.
examples: We recycle cans and paper.
We recycle old boxes.
You can recycle glass jars.

more.def: To turn used materials into something new instead of throwing them away.
examples: Our school recycles plastic bottles to help keep the Earth clean.
The factory recycles old tires into playground mats.
Remember to recycle the newspaper when you finish it.

easy.def: Having the color of an apple or a fire truck.
examples: The apple is red.
A fire truck is red.
She wore a red hat.

more.def: Having the color of blood, ripe tomatoes or fire trucks.
examples: A red cardinal sat in the snowy tree.
The sunset turned the sky red and orange.
His cheeks were red from the cold wind.

easy.def: The color of an apple or a fire truck.
examples: Red is my favorite color.
Mix red and yellow to make orange.
The leaves turned to red.

more.def: The color of ripe tomatoes, strawberries and fire trucks.
examples: The artist painted the barn in bright red.
Red means stop on a traffic light.
The flag has stripes of red and white.

easy.def: To show a picture back, like a mirror does.
examples: The lake reflects the trees.
The mirror reflects my face.
Snow reflects the sun.

more.def: To throw back light, heat, sound, or an image from a surface.
examples: The calm water reflected the mountains like a mirror.
The shiny window reflected the sunlight.
A white roof reflects heat and keeps the house cool.

related.def: A thing that sends light back.

examples: I refuse to eat peas.
She refused the cake.
He refused to go.

more.def: To say that you will not do or accept something.
examples: I refuse to eat the spinach.
She refused the offer of a ride.
The cat refused to come out from under the bed.

easy.def: To put a name on a list.
examples: I registered for the class.
We registered for camp.
He registered his name.

more.def: To sign up or put your name on an official list.
examples: Children registered for soccer at the park.
She registered her new bike with the police.
We registered at the front desk of the hotel.
The teacher marked the register.
Sign the register.
The register shows who is here.

more.def: An official list or record of names or events.
examples: The teacher took the register each morning.
Visitors sign the hotel register.
The old register listed every child in the town.
I regret my words.
She regrets breaking the vase.
He regretted yelling.

more.def: To feel sorry about something you did or did not do.
examples: I regret saying those unkind words.
She regrets forgetting her friend's birthday.
He regretted leaving his coat at home.

easy.def: A sad feeling about something you did.
examples: I feel regret.
Her regret was clear.
He had no regrets.

more.def: A feeling of sadness about something you did or did not do.
examples: She felt deep regret about the lost toy.
He has no regrets about the trip.
Her regret showed on her face.
It's a regular day.
Our regular teacher.
A regular size.

more.def: Normal, usual or happening again and again.
examples: We have a regular class every Friday.
She ordered a regular size pizza.
The bus makes regular stops.

easy.def: How two people get along or are connected.
examples: My sister and I have a close relationship.
The two dogs have a good relationship.
A teacher and student have a relationship.

more.def: The way that two people or things are connected or feel about each other.
examples: She has a warm relationship with her grandfather.
Scientists study the relationship between plants and bees.
Brothers and sisters often have a close relationship.
I relax with a good book.
The cat relaxes in the sun.
We relax at the beach.

more.def: To rest and become calm and less worried.
examples: After the test, the students could finally relax.
A warm bath helps me relax.
Relax your shoulders and take a deep breath.
Release the bird.
He released the balloon.
The zoo released the animal.

more.def: To let a person or animal go free, or to let go of something.
examples: The girl released the butterfly into the garden.
The park ranger released the fish back into the river.
He released the balloon and watched it float up.
Remain in your seat.
The cat remained still.
Only one cookie remained.

more.def: To stay in the same place or condition.
examples: Please remain in your seats.
The cat remained still all afternoon.
Only one cookie remained on the plate.

easy.def: To keep something in your mind.
examples: I remember my first day of school.
Do you remember my name?
I remember the way home.

more.def: To bring something back into your mind, or to not forget it.
examples: Remember to bring your lunch on the field trip.
I cannot remember where I put my keys.
She still remembers the song her grandmother taught her.
Remind me to call.
She reminded me.
Please remind him.

more.def: To make someone remember something.
examples: Please remind me to bring my gym shoes.
My alarm reminds me to feed the fish.
She reminded him about the test.

easy.def: To make someone think of something.
examples: You remind me of my sister.
This song reminds me of summer.
The smell reminds me of baking.

more.def: To make someone think of a person, place or thing.
examples: That song reminds me of our trip.
The smell of pine reminds her of winter.
You remind me of my cousin.
Remove your shoes.
She removed the lid.
He removes the trash.

more.def: To take something away from a place.
examples: Please remove your shoes at the door.
She removed the lid from the pot.
Workers removed the fallen tree.
We rent a house.
They rented a bike.
She rents a room.

more.def: To pay money to use something that belongs to someone else.
examples: We rent a cabin every summer.
They rented bikes for the day.
My aunt rents an apartment in the city.
The rent is due.
We pay rent each month.
The rent is high.

more.def: Money you pay regularly to use a house, room or thing.
examples: We pay the rent on the first of the month.
The rent for the apartment is high.
She paid the rent for the cabin.
Please repeat that.
The parrot repeats words.
Repeat after me.

more.def: To say or do something again.
examples: Please repeat the question.
The parrot repeats everything I say.
Repeat the steps until the dough is smooth.

easy.def: To put a new thing where an old one was.
examples: I need to replace my shoes.
We replaced the bulb.
Please replace the broken cup.

more.def: To take the place of something, or to put a new thing in place of one that is gone or broken.
examples: Dad replaced the old light bulb with a new one.
The teacher replaced the cracked ruler.
Please replace the books on the shelf when you finish.

easy.def: Writing or talking that tells about something.
examples: I wrote a report on whales.
The weather report says rain.
She gave a report to the class.

more.def: A written or spoken description of a subject, an event or something you have studied.
examples: I wrote a report about the planets for science class.
The weather report says it will snow tonight.
A report from the park said that the bridge was open.
The paper reports the score.
Please report a lost jacket to the office.
She reported the news to her class.

more.def: To give information about something, especially what you have seen, heard or studied.
examples: Scientists reported that the ice is melting slowly.
Please report any broken equipment to your coach.
The newspaper reported on the parade.

easy.def: A person who tells the news.
examples: The reporter wrote a story.
A reporter asked questions.
She is a news reporter.

more.def: A person whose job is to gather and tell the news.
examples: The reporter wrote a story about the parade.
A TV reporter stood outside the school.
A reporter asked the mayor questions.
The flag represents our country.
A heart represents love.
The red stands for stop.

more.def: To stand for or be a sign of something.
examples: The eagle represents freedom in many stories.
A heart often represents love.
Each star on the flag represents a state.

easy.def: To speak or act for others.
examples: She represents our class.
He represents our school.
The lawyer represents her.

more.def: To speak or act for a group or another person.
examples: She represents our class on the student council.
The lawyer represented the family in court.
He represents our school at the contest.

easy.def: An animal with dry skin and scales, like a snake.
examples: A turtle is a reptile.
A snake is a reptile.
The reptile sat in the sun.

more.def: A cold-blooded animal with dry, scaly skin that usually lays eggs.
examples: Snakes, lizards, and crocodiles are all reptiles.
Reptiles warm their bodies in the sun.
The reptile house at the zoo has lizards and turtles.
I request a song.
She requested more water.
He requested a seat.

more.def: To ask for something politely or formally.
examples: I requested a book from the library.
She requested a window seat.
The teacher requested quiet.
I have a request.
The request was granted.
She made a request.

more.def: A polite or formal asking for something.
examples: The singer played our request.
I made a request for extra time.
Her request for a window seat was granted.

more.def: To need something, or to say that something must be done.
examples: Plants require water and sunlight.
This game requires two players.
The school requires uniforms.
The firefighter will rescue the cat from the tree.

We rescued a kitten from the rain.

more.def: To save someone or something from danger or harm.
examples: A lifeguard rescued the swimmer who was too tired to reach the shore.

I did research for my report.
Scientists do research.
The research took days.

more.def: Careful study to find facts about something.
examples: I did research for my report on whales.
Scientists do research in the lab.
The research took several weeks.
I research frogs.
She researched the topic.
He researches bats.

more.def: To study something carefully to find facts.
examples: I researched owls for my project.
She researched the history of her town.
Scientists research ways to clean the ocean.

easy.def: Being nice and caring about how others feel.
examples: We show respect when we listen.
We treat our teacher with respect.
Show respect for the park. Do not litter.

more.def: A feeling that someone or something is important and should be treated well.
examples: We show respect for our classmates by listening when they speak.
The players shook hands as a sign of respect.
She has great respect for her grandfather.
I respond to the email.
She responded to the question.
The dog responds to its name.

more.def: To say or do something in answer to something else.
examples: He responded to the teacher's question with a smile.
The dog responds quickly when you call its name.

Feeding the pet is my responsibility.

more.def: Something that is your job to do or take care of.
examples: Feeding the fish is my responsibility.

The teacher has a big responsibility.

easy.def: Doing the things you are supposed to do.
examples: I am responsible for feeding my cat.

He is responsible for the class pet.

more.def: Able to be trusted to do what is right or what you are supposed to do.
examples: A responsible pet owner makes sure the dog gets a walk every day.

easy.def: To stop and be still after you were busy.
examples: I rest on the couch.
The dog rested.
Let us rest here.

more.def: To stop working or moving so that your body can get strong again.
examples: We sat down to rest after the long hike.

The cat rested in a patch of sunshine.
I ate the rest.

She kept the rest.

more.def: The part that is left over, or the other people or things.
examples: I ate one cookie and saved the rest for later.

easy.def: A place where you buy a meal and eat it there.

more.def: A place where people pay to sit and eat meals that are cooked for them.

more.def: To happen because of something else.
examples: The heavy rain resulted in a flood.

more.def: To stop working at a job, usually because of age.
examples: My grandfather retired after forty years as a mail carrier.
The famous baseball player will retire at the end of the season.

easy.def: To go back to a place.

more.def: To go or come back to a place.
examples: The birds return to the north every spring.

more.def: To give, send or put something back where it came from.

more.def: To look over or study something again so that you remember it.
examples: We reviewed our spelling words before the test.

easy.def: Writing about a book or movie you saw.

more.def: A report that tells what someone thinks of a book, movie or show.
examples: The newspaper gave the movie a good review.

more.def: Something given to you for doing something good or helpful.
